::: {.proj-layout}
::: {.proj-main}
::: {.proj-question}
## Research question

Is concentrated solar power with thermal storage feeding high-temperature electrolysis more economic than photovoltaics feeding low-temperature electrolysis in West Texas?
:::

::: {.proj-pair}
::: {.proj-col}
## My contribution

First author. Added a concentrated-solar module to the REopt-based model and ran the analysis.
:::

::: {.proj-col}
## Method

Optimization of a 115-MW solar plant with electrolysis using SAM solar models, ERCOT prices and ATB cost trajectories.
:::

:::

::: {.proj-findings}
## Key findings

::: {.findings}
1. Among the cases studied, concentrated solar power with thermal storage running the electrolyzer at variable power gave the lowest levelized hydrogen cost; constant-power operation was the most expensive.
:::
:::

::: {.proj-bounds}
## Boundary conditions

Single West Texas site; cost trajectories from NREL's Annual Technology Baseline; conference-length study.
:::

:::
